data_quality_notes:
Research ran to completion and logged a RESEARCH COMPLETE block - nothing here is truncated. 7 candidate lines resolved to 5 distinct symbols (UAL and PCG were each re-captured to remove an invented catalyst timestamp; the last line per symbol is used). All 5 published, 0 dropped on the reward-to-risk floor: every ratio below was recomputed here from the final entry, target and downside rather than taken from the notes - IWM 3.50, PCG 2.97, LULU 2.62, GLNG 2.62, UAL 2.39, each against its horizon floor (2.0 swing / 2.5 long-term). The two closest to their floor (LULU and GLNG at 2.62) get there because the entry was set 7-15% below the market, not because a target was raised to fit, which is the failure mode this check exists to catch.

PRICES: every quote is the 2026-08-31 close, fetched pre-open via finnhub and roughly 870 minutes old. That is a closed market, not stale data - at 6am ET the previous close is the freshest honest equity price. No price here is estimated.

FEEDS THAT FAILED, and what it cost: yahoo returned HTTP 429 on every index symbol all morning, finnhub refuses index CFDs, stooq 404'd, alphavantage has no key. So there is no live VIX, DXY, ^GSPC/^NDX/^DJI/^RUT, gold or WTI quote in this report, and ETF proxies (SPY/QQQ/IWM/GLD/XLE/TLT) stand in for the index levels. Two direct consequences: there is no futures idea today, and the index short is IWM rather than the /M2K contract config/universe.md prefers - quoting futures levels that could not be fetched would be a fabrication, so the ETF carries requires_margin: true instead. Brent 90.91 and WTI 85.02 in market_context.levels come from news reporting, not a fetched quote, and are labelled as such.

WHY THE MIX IS WHAT IT IS: 3 long-term, 2 swing, 0 intraday, and the skew is deliberate rather than a shortfall. Nothing intraday cleared the bar - with equities closed and the index and VIX feeds down, there was no honest way to set an intraday level. Zero event contracts publish despite three ladders being priced and worked through in full (Kalshi September Fed 57/58c, August CPI YoY, September AAA gas): each estimated edge landed inside the modelling error or inside the spread, so all three were rejected on the same standard. That is a result, not a coverage gap.

CONCENTRATION IS THE REPORT'S BIGGEST RISK, and it is not in any single idea. New ideas respect the 3-per-driver cap (Hormuz/oil: UAL short and GLNG long; Fed hikes: IWM short; idiosyncratic: LULU, PCG). The combined book does not - XLE x3 + DINO + UAL + GLNG is six lines on the same war. Separately, the IWM short and the SPY short published 08/31 at 773 are one macro bet expressed twice and should be sized as a single position.

POSITION BOOKKEEPING, which the track record depends on: TJX and all four BTC / /MBTU6 shorts are past their stops and are marked CLOSED at their stops, not carried - TJX at 145.50 (-3.5%) with the last print 8.0% through it, and the BTC shorts stopped weeks ago against a 77,889 spot. DINO, XLE, TJX and BCC appear on the watchlist as open-position management notes rather than recommendations, because their R:R as new entries is below floor (DINO at 101.61 into a 95.00 stop and a 108 target is 0.97) and the floor exists to reject ideas, not to calibrate targets.

Four of the five ideas carry wait: true. That is the honest read of a tape where the entries worth having are all away from the current price - it is not hedging.

NOT REACHED: Asia/Europe overnight tape, an SEC 8-K sweep beyond GLNG, small-cap screening beyond the fertilizer and defense names, and crypto beyond spot prices. Documented rejections with reasoning are in notes.md: EQT/AR/RRC, CF, LXU, UAN, AVAV, KTOS, PBF/VLO (correlation cap only - the crack-spread case is good and there is simply no room), FRO/INSW/TNK, GIS, CPB, GLD, and the three event ladders. Finally, the track record behind this report is 0/9 closed trades at target and n=9 is noise - do not over-fit to it in either direction.

RED TEAM (phase 2c), a separate pass that did not write the above and owes it nothing. Three of five ideas cut to the watchlist with reasons, one downgraded, one untouched; two recommendations survive. Every level in the original report was recomputed from source first and all of them check out exactly - IWM 20/50/200-day at 300.14/297.28/271.56, UAL at 120.47/123.05/108.03, GLNG 200-day 47.05, LULU 200-day 153.84, and every ATR - so nothing here is a levels dispute. CUT PCG (rank 4) on the evidence, which is the only kill that turns on a fact the report did not have: its thesis is that the 20% selloff overreacted because only fund mechanics changed, but PG&E's own published statement on SB 492 says the bill 'does not adequately address the financing risks created by California's current wildfire liability framework', and Mizuho reads it as victim protection with no investor protection. The idea conceded it could not verify the AB 1054 question; the issuer has effectively answered it the wrong way. CUT GLNG (rank 3): good research, not a trade today. At the market price its ratio is 1.85 and fails the 2.5 floor, and the published 2.62 exists only because the entry was placed 14.5% below market - a level that mostly prints in the world where Hormuz reopens and the thesis is dead. Moving an entry down to clear the floor is the same failure as moving a target up, and the mechanical spread check failed it at 6.16% as well. CUT UAL (rank 5) on the correlation test: with XLE x3 and DINO already long the oil shock, a short UAL on jet fuel is the sixth line on one war and dies on the same ceasefire headline - and it was the weakest of that cluster, with no dated catalyst, a target 6.01 ATR out on a 15-session horizon, and a bear case its own counter-argument calls fully public. DOWNGRADED IWM from conviction 3 to 2 and from 2% to 1% (the conviction-2 sizing cap), and dropped it to rank 2. Its 3.50 ratio is geometry, not edge - a 2.47 ATR stop against an 8.65 ATR target - and the target cannot be pulled in without failing the swing floor, so the conviction moved rather than the number. It is also void on a 51%-probability event three sessions before its own catalyst, and the hike odds it rests on are quoted between 48% and 66% across public sources on the same day. Left standing rather than killed because the entry, stop and stand-down rule are all specific and defensible. KEPT LULU at conviction 3 unchanged, and it is now rank 1: it is the only idea here with a company-confirmed dated catalyst (09/03 after the close, verified from lululemon's own 08/20 release), a falsifiable bar management set itself, and an entry zone a post-print gap can actually reach - unlike the two entries above, a 112 print on 09/03 is plausible precisely when the thesis is being tested rather than when it is already dead. No criticism was manufactured to pad this list, and the concentration warning in the original notes was correct and is the reason two of the three cuts happened.

market_context.summary: The tape is pricing stagflation directly, and that is the frame for every idea below. Kalshi puts a 57-58c probability on a 25bp Fed HIKE on 09/16 (CME FedWatch 60.4%) after Chair Warsh's 08/28 Jackson Hole keynote recommitted to the 2% PCE target, while the same market prices a 51% chance August unemployment rises to 4.2%+ from 4.1% - a policy rate going up into a weakening labour market. The driver is a live US-Iran war now in month six: US strikes on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on 08/30 put Brent at 90.91 (+3.2%) and US national average gasoline stayed above $4/gal every day of August for the first time ever. Breadth on 08/31 says the same thing - XLE +2.04% while IWM -0.62% and SPY -0.30% with QQQ flat, which is commodity and inflation leadership, not risk-on. The 10Y at 4.73% against a 3.63% effective funds rate is a term-premium and fiscal story rather than a growth story, and GLD at 408 near its high is beating a Fed the market thinks hikes in two weeks. The week's event is Friday's 08:30 ET jobs report, which cuts both ways: a rising unemployment rate collapses the hike odds near term while confirming the growth problem.

recommendations.thesis: Update to the 2026-08-22 long opened at 115 (last 120.26, +4.6%): thesis intact, HOLD, do not add before the 09/03 print. At 120.26 LULU trades near 10.9x the low end of its own reset FY26 guidance of 10.95-11.15 EPS, a multiple normally reserved for a structurally broken retailer rather than a brand still earning 55%-plus gross margins with no meaningful net debt. The June cut already took the number down roughly 10 percent, so 09/03 is judged against a bar management set itself rather than the pre-cut consensus that drove the 42 percent year-to-date de-rating.
recommendations.key_risk: The problem is demand-side, not cost-side — management blamed negative brand commentary and weak product launches — so a second consecutive guidance cut on 09/03 would confirm the de-rating is earnings-driven rather than multiple-driven. Positioning into the print is crowded: 08/31 traded 13.65M shares against a 4.2M average, which is how a miss gaps rather than drifts. Explicit invalidation: a second consecutive guidance cut, FY27 EPS guided below 9.00, or gross margin below 52 percent for two consecutive quarters; bear-case value 88 is 11x on 8.00 of EPS.
recommendations.counter_argument: Athleisure brands rarely recover a premium multiple once the culture moves on — Under Armour spent a decade cheap and never re-rated. Buying 11x on the assumption the multiple returns is a bet on taste, and if North America comps stay negative alongside China softness, FY27 EPS toward 8.00 puts the stock at 88 with nothing structural underneath it.

recommendations.counter_argument: Three things sit against this, and the first is structural. The 3.50 reward-to-risk is a product of the geometry rather than an edge: the stop sits 2.47 ATR above entry while the target sits 8.65 ATR below it, and validation flags that target as beyond the 6.0 ATR guide for a 15-session swing. IWM has not closed below 290 in 130 sessions, so 274 is the only defensible target on the chart - it sits just above the 200-day at 271.56 with real air above it - but reaching it means breaking a six-month range inside three weeks in an index with a 0.96% daily ATR. Pulling the target in to something reachable (285, about 4.8 ATR) drops the ratio to 1.93 and fails the 2.0 swing floor outright. That tension is the honest state of the idea: the number was not massaged, so the conviction comes down instead. Second, the trade is more likely than not to be cancelled before its own catalyst ever arrives - entry requires a bounce into 296.50-301.50, and the stand-down rule voids it if the 09/04 jobs report shows a rising unemployment rate, which this report's own market context prices at 51%. Third, the hike is not the firm 57-60% the thesis leans on. Public sources on 08/31 put it anywhere from 48% (CNBC, citing Kalshi) to 60.4% and 66.1% (CME FedWatch, in two different write-ups), and CNBC's own headline is that not everyone is convinced. It is a coin flip that is already half in the price, and IWM is only 3.7% off its 52-week high - an orderly pullback, not a breakdown. If the Fed holds, or if Treasury Secretary Bessent wins the public argument that you do not raise into a supply shock, small caps are the highest-beta thing to a relief rally and this is the wrong side of a 5% gap. Finally it still stacks with the SPY short published 08/31 at 773: size the two as one macro position, not two.

watchlist.note: Cut from rank 4 by red team, on the evidence rather than the arithmetic. The thesis was that the 20.1% selloff to 13.27 prices a step-change in liability exposure when what actually changed was fund mechanics - i.e. an overreaction. The issuer says the opposite. PG&E's own statement on SB 492 is that the bill 'does not adequately address the financing risks created by California's current wildfire liability framework' and 'falls short of creating the long-term durability needed to attract affordable investment', citing the California Earthquake Authority's April finding that existing funding mechanisms are not sufficient. Mizuho reads it the same way: SB 492 is victim protection (fast-pay, a ban on selling claims to private equity, executive-comp limits) with no new investor protection. The idea's own key_risk conceded it could not verify whether the AB 1054 cap survives; the publicly available answer is that the company itself considers the framework unresolved, which is not the profile of a market overreaction. Zero insider open-market buys against 9 sales worth $6.36M in six months points the same way, in a company that already wiped out its equity on this exact mechanism in 2019. Sources: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/PCG/pg-e-statement-on-senate-bill-4oj1tv3xhedb.html , https://seekingalpha.com/news/4638568-california-lawmakers-set-to-vote-on-wildfire-liability-bill
watchlist.trigger: The passed SB 492 text actually read, confirming the AB 1054 liability cap (20% of T&D equity rate base for a utility holding a valid safety certification) survives intact - or a follow-on bill that caps, funds and replenishes the wildfire fund. The reaffirmed $1.64-1.66 FY26 core EPS, $73B capital plan to 2030 and no-dilution commitment make the equity cheap at 8.0x if and only if liability is capped; uncapped, the 9.50 bear case is generous. If the fund stays uncapped and unreplenished with insurers still able to subrogate, there is no trade here at any price.
watchlist.demotion_reason: The issuer's own public statement on SB 492 contradicts the 'market overreacted on fund mechanics' thesis the target rests on.
